newsitem.title: USA: US rail carloads, ton-miles up from year ago -- AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail carloads, ton-miles up from year ago -- AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in carloads and ton-miles rose in the week ended January 25 from the same week a year ago but intermodal fell, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said carloads last week totaled 332,060, up two percent from 325,459 in the year-ago week. Ton-miles rose 2.4 percent to 26.1 billion from 25.5 billion a year ago. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
But AAR said intermodal volume, which does not include carloads, fell 0.7 percent in the week to 158,358 trailers and containers from 159,465 a year ago.

AAR said carloads of metallic ores posted the largest gains from last year, up 20 percent to 14,359 from 11,966. Loadings of metals and related products also climbed 15.8 percent from last year to 13,348 carloads from 11,530.

Petroleum carloads were 5,635 in the week, a nine percent increase from 5,170 in the year-ago week. AAR reported 1,544 carloads of farm products other than grain, up five percent from 1,471 a year ago. Grain mill products also increased 6.1 percent to 9,515 from 8,971 last year.
But nonmetallic minerals loadings fell 10.3 percent in the week to 8,067 from 8,994 last year, while primary forest products dipped 6.1 percent to 7,150 carloads from 7,611.
Grain loadings fell only 0.1 percent to 27,080 carloads in the week from 27,105 in the year-ago week.
In the first four weeks of 1997, AAR said that ton-miles rose 3.9 percent from the same 1996 period. Carloads rose 2.7 percent and intermodal freight rose three percent, it said.

In a separate accounting, AAR said U.S. intermodal traffic to Canada in the January 25 week totaled 22,661 trailers and containers, up seven percent from the year-ago week. It said U.S. carloads to Canada were 50,246, down 0.1 percent from a year ago.
